questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Build Configuration”?
options: Build Configuration means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Build Configuration removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Build Configuration should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Build Configuration helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Build Configuration helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Build Configuration is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “angular.json build settings” in this lesson?
options: Assume “angular.json build settings” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “angular.json build settings” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “angular.json build settings” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “angular.json build settings” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “angular.json build settings” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “angular.json build settings” under Build Configuration. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Build Configuration”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
